featuredPost.title: Introducing QuickPDF 2.0: Faster, Smarter, and Completely Redesigned
featuredPost.excerpt: Today we're thrilled to announce the biggest update in our history. We've rebuilt QuickPDF from the ground up to provide a blazing fast, ultra-secure, and beautifully designed experience for all your document needs.
featuredPost.content:
Today we're thrilled to announce the biggest update in our history. We've rebuilt QuickPDF from the ground up to provide a blazing fast, ultra-secure, and beautifully designed experience for all your document needs.

What's new in 2.0?

Over the last six months, our team has been hard at work addressing your most requested features and completely overhauling our processing engine. Here are the highlights of what you can expect:

  • Client-side Processing: Many of our tools now process your files directly in your browser without ever uploading them to our servers, resulting in instant results and absolute privacy.
  • A Brand New Interface: We've completely redesigned our UI to be cleaner, faster, and more intuitive. Every tool is now just a single click away.
  • Batch Processing: You can now drag and drop dozens of files at once. QuickPDF will process them in parallel and download them as a convenient ZIP file.

Under the Hood

We didn't just change how QuickPDF looks; we fundamentally changed how it works. By migrating to a robust Next.js frontend combined with highly optimized WebAssembly (Wasm) modules for PDF manipulation, we've reduced processing times by up to 80% on average.

"Our goal was simple: build the fastest PDF tool on the web without compromising an inch on security or user experience."

What's Next?

This is just the beginning. Over the coming weeks, we'll be rolling out our highly anticipated AI features, including the ability to chat with your PDFs and automatically summarize long documents. Stay tuned!

blogPosts.content:
Securing your documents is more important now than ever. Here is how you can ensure your PDFs are safe.

1. Use Strong Passwords

Always use AES-256 encryption when exporting your PDFs. QuickPDF automatically uses this standard when you use our Protect PDF tool.

blogPosts.title: The Ultimate Guide to Compressing Large PDF Files
blogPosts.excerpt: Struggling to send a large PDF over email? Discover our top tips for reducing file size without losing quality.
blogPosts.content:
Email attachments can be frustrating. Here is how you can shrink those PDFs down to a manageable size.

Understanding Compression

Most of the size in a PDF comes from unoptimized images. By downscaling images to 144 DPI, you can save massive amounts of space without noticeable quality loss on screens.

blogPosts.title: Why We Switched to a Fully Client-Side Architecture
blogPosts.excerpt: A deep dive into our engineering decisions and how processing files on your device drastically improves speed and privacy.
blogPosts.content:
Moving from the server to the browser was the best engineering decision we ever made.

WebAssembly is the Future

By compiling our C++ PDF libraries to WebAssembly, we eliminated the need to upload files entirely. Your documents never leave your computer.
